introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.
incertitudes: Q20 passée en ouverte : « Voulez-vous » (B) et « Voudriez-vous » (D) sont tous deux corrects ; A (« Voudrez ») n'existe pas et C (« Veuillez ») est incompatible avec le « -vous » inversé. Aucune lettre désignée.
Q24 passée en ouverte : l'expression attendue est « a fait fortune », mais l'option D est imprimée « s'est fait fortune » (fautive) ; aucune autre option ne convient. Aucune lettre désignée.

Q45 passée en ouverte : la consigne est ambiguë (le « Si » initial peut être le « si » de réponse affirmative à une question négative, d'où D, ou le « si » d'une interrogation indirecte, d'où A ou B). Aucune lettre désignée.
Q48 passée en ouverte : A « des branches », B « de l'herbe » et D « l'herbe » sont tous défendables après « coupe » pour des moutons et chèvres ; aucune lettre désignée.

Q50 passée en ouverte : « bain » (B), « douche » (D) et, plus largement, « toilette » (A) conviennent (aucun déterminant imprimé avant le blanc) ; seule « bouteille » est exclue. Aucune lettre désignée.

Clés retenues mais à relire : Q1 c La (« Une » est grammaticalement possible mais moins précis), Q12 a peureux (d faibles est plus faible comme antonyme de courageux), Q28 b festivals (d fêtes est défendable), Q39 a Il faut parler peu (la maxime est mal rendue par les 4 options, a est la moins fausse), Q49 b petit déjeuner (a déjeuner pourrait désigner un repas emporté), Q27 a avant de (d sans aussi grammatical mais illogique).

Q41 : l'option C est imprimée avec une majuscule (« S'être habillés »), erreur d'impression retenue comme seule forme grammaticale ; Q47 : l'option A est imprimée « à u » (recopiée telle quelle) ; Q22 : l'option B est imprimée « les notres » sans accent (recopiée telle quelle) ; Q13 : option C « quelqu' » recopiée telle quelle.
Q17 et Q44 sont des questions de traduction (anglais/français) glissées parmi les questions de grammaire ; thème « translation into French ».

Scan photocopié avec filigrane (gcerevision.com) ignoré, ainsi que la publicité imprimée en haut et en bas de page : accents et élisions relus sur un rendu à 200 dpi, aucune zone illisible. Les blancs imprimés en traits sont écrits « ____ » ou conservés tels quels quand l'impression est en tirets ; les mots soulignés du sujet (Q11, Q15) sont balisés par <u>...</u> ; les numéros soulignés du passage 46-50 sont écrits (46) à (50).

questions.enonce_markdown: ____ fille qui est assise à la véranda est ma sœur.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence points to a particular girl, already identified by the relative clause "qui est assise à la véranda", so the definite article "la" (feminine singular) is used. "Cet" is masculine, and "L'" is only used before a vowel. "Une" is grammatical but introduces an unidentified girl, which does not suit a precise identification. Rule: a known, identified noun takes the definite article. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Quels ____ cheveux !
questions.corrige_markdown: "Cheveux" is masculine plural, so the exclamative needs "beaux". "Beau" and "bel" are singular and "belles" is feminine. Rule: the adjective agrees in gender and number with its noun. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Veuillez nous servir ____ jus.
questions.corrige_markdown: We ask for an unspecified quantity of juice, so the partitive article "du" (de + le) is used: "servir du jus". "De" alone is only used after a negation or an expression of quantity, and "le" or "les" would designate specific juices. Rule: the partitive du, de la, des expresses an indefinite quantity. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Vous me remboursez ____ francs.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Cent" takes an -s when it is multiplied (cinq cents) and not followed by another number; here it ends the number, so "cinq cents francs". "Cinq cent" lacks the -s, "cinq cents cinquante" wrongly keeps the -s before another number, and a hyphen is not used before a noun. Rule: cents takes -s only when it is not followed by another number. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - numbers and fractions

questions.enonce_markdown: Quand j'ai pris le téléphone, ____ voix féminine m'a parlé.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Voix" is feminine and the speaker is unknown, so the indefinite article "une" is used: "une voix féminine". "Un" is masculine, "la" would suppose a voice already identified and "certaine" is an adjective that cannot stand alone here. Rule: an unidentified noun takes the indefinite article, in agreement with its gender. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Le professeur ne viendra pas ____ il est malade.
questions.corrige_markdown: The second clause explains why the teacher will not come, so the causal conjunction "car" (because) is required. "Donc" gives a consequence, "or" introduces an argument and "mais" opposes two ideas. Rule: car = because. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cet élève parle ____ français.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Parler couramment une langue" means to speak it fluently, which is the natural collocation. "Courageusement" (bravely), "courtoisement" (politely) and "complètement" (completely) do not describe how well one speaks a language. Rule: parler couramment = to speak fluently. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Il a retroussé ____ de sa chemise.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Retrousser" means to roll up, and what one rolls up on a shirt is the sleeve, "la manche" (feminine). "Le manche" is the handle of a tool, and one does not roll up "la main" or "le bras" of a shirt. Rule: la manche = sleeve, le manche = handle. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Nous ____ toujours les cours à sept heures trente.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Toujours" shows a habit in the present, so the present indicative of "commencer" with "nous" is used. In the nous form the c becomes ç before o to keep the soft sound: "commençons". "Commencons" lacks the cedilla, "commencent" is for ils/elles and "avons commencé" is a past tense. Rule: verbs in -cer take ç before a and o. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: ____ médecin après mes études.
questions.corrige_markdown: The possessive "mes études" shows that the speaker is the subject, so the first person singular future "Je serai" is needed. The other options have a different subject (tu, elle, il) or a conditional. Rule: the subject must match the possessive (mes goes with je). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: La <u>bonne hygiène</u> nous éloigne des maladies. Le mot souligné a pour synonyme :
questions.corrige_markdown: "Hygiène" refers to cleanliness and healthy conditions, which is close to "salubrité" (healthiness). "Insalubrité" is the opposite, "sobriété" means moderation and "extrémité" means end or extreme. Rule: salubrité = state of being healthy. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Dans l'armée on recrute les hommes courageux et jamais les ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: The blank must be the opposite of "courageux"; the direct antonym is "peureux" (fearful). "Généreux" and "éveillés" have nothing to do with courage, and "faibles" (weak) refers to physical strength rather than courage. Rule: courageux has the antonym peureux. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Elle admirait ____ image dans un miroir.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Image" is feminine but begins with a vowel, so the feminine possessive "sa" is replaced by "son" to avoid a hiatus: "son image". "Sa image" is incorrect, "un" is masculine and "quelqu'" is incomplete (it would need "quelque" or "quelqu'une"). Rule: before a feminine noun starting with a vowel, ma, ta, sa become mon, ton, son. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Qu'est-ce que vous faites ____ au fond de la classe ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The question asks what the pupils are doing at the back of the classroom, a place seen at a distance, so the adverb of place "là-bas" (over there) fits. "Jadis" is an adverb of time, "ci-bas" belongs to the phrase "ici-bas" and "là-haut" suggests a higher place. Rule: là-bas indicates a distant place. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Ils sont arrivés à l'école à <u>sept heures et quart</u>. Le groupe de mots soulignés veut dire qu'ils y sont arrivés à :
questions.corrige_markdown: "Et quart" means plus fifteen minutes, so "sept heures et quart" is 7:15, i.e. "sept heures quinze minutes". Options A and C are 19:15 (7:15 p.m.), and "huit heures moins vingt" is 7:40. Rule: et quart = +15 minutes, et demie = +30, moins le quart = -15. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - numbers and fractions

questions.enonce_markdown: -------- -vous comporter en milieu scolaire !
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence is an order addressed to "vous", so the imperative second person plural of "savoir" is used: "Sachez vous comporter". "Sache" is the tu form, "sachons" the nous form and "savoir" the infinitive. Rule: the imperative with vous ends in -ez, here irregular (sachez). **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: L'expression « Cela m'est égal. » se traduit en anglais par :
questions.corrige_markdown: "Cela m'est égal" is an idiom meaning that one has no preference, i.e. "It makes no difference to me". The other options translate the words literally or give a different meaning. Rule: cela m'est égal = I don't mind. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - translation into French

choix.texte: It makes no difference to me.

questions.enonce_markdown: Paul et sa sœur ____ tôt ce matin.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Se lever" is pronominal and uses the auxiliary "être"; the past participle agrees with the reflexive pronoun, which is the direct object. The subject "Paul et sa sœur" is mixed, so the masculine plural wins: "se sont levés". "Ont levé" has the wrong auxiliary, "levées" is feminine and "levé" is not in the plural. Rule: in mixed groups the masculine plural prevails. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Le président voyagera ____ en Italie.
questions.corrige_markdown: The verb is in the future ("voyagera"), so the adverb of time must refer to the future: "demain" (tomorrow). "Maintenant" (now) and "tout de suite" (right now) refer to the present, and "auparavant" (before) to the past. Rule: the time adverb agrees with the tense. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown:
----------- -vous me permettre de sortir, monsieur ?

*Options as printed:* A) Voudrez B) Voulez C) Veuillez D) Voudriez
questions.corrige_markdown: Option A "Voudrez" does not exist and option C "Veuillez" cannot be followed by an inverted "-vous". Two options remain correct: "Voulez-vous me permettre de sortir, monsieur ?" (present, a normal polite question) and "Voudriez-vous me permettre de sortir, monsieur ?" (conditional, more courteous, the form a pupil would use with a teacher). Since both B and D are defensible, no letter is designated. Rule: the conditional softens a request.
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Voici le monsieur ____ le chien est mort.
questions.corrige_markdown: The relative clause needs a pronoun meaning "whose": "le chien du monsieur" becomes "dont le chien". "Que" is a direct object, "lequel" cannot replace a possessive link and "donc" is a conjunction. Rule: dont replaces de + noun and expresses possession. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mon père nous a acheté un téléviseur, une imprimante et un ordinateur. Tous ces appareils sont ----------.
questions.corrige_markdown: The father bought them for "nous", so the devices belong to us: the possessive pronoun is "les nôtres", with a circumflex and the definite article. "Les notres" lacks the accent, "nos" is a determiner and cannot stand alone after "sont", and "les leurs" means theirs. Rule: possessive pronoun for nous = le/la/les nôtre(s). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: La drogue est------pour la santé.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Drogue" is feminine singular, so the adjective must be feminine: "dangereuse". "Dangereux" and "mauvais" are masculine, and "danger" is a noun. Rule: the attribute adjective agrees with its subject. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown:
Il ________ avec le petit commerce.

*Options as printed:* A) a fait la queue B) a fait les courses C) a fait les affaires D) s'est fait fortune
questions.corrige_markdown: The intended expression is "faire fortune" (to become rich): "Il a fait fortune avec le petit commerce". The printed option D, "s'est fait fortune", is ungrammatical ("faire fortune" is not reflexive; one would say "il s'est enrichi" or "il a fait fortune"), and none of the other options means to become rich (queue = waiting line, courses = shopping, "faire les affaires" is not standard). Because no printed option is correct, no letter is designated. Rule: faire fortune = to get rich.

questions.enonce_markdown: Jeunes écoliers, nous ______ jusqu'à tard dans la nuit.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Jeunes écoliers" recalls a past habit, so the imperfect of "étudier" with "nous" is used: the stem "étudi-" plus the ending -ions gives "étudiions". "Étudierions" is conditional, "étudierons" future and "étudions" present. Rule: the imperfect nous form keeps the i of the stem before -ions. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Allez-vous à Yaoundé ? Non ---------------reviens plutôt.
questions.corrige_markdown: The pronoun "en" replaces "de + place" (the place I come from): "j'en reviens" means I have just come back from there. "J'y" replaces "à + place" and would mean I am going back there, and "je m'en" and "je l'en" are not possible with "reviens". Rule: en replaces de + place after a verb of return. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Manges-tu ______ te laver les mains ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The preposition must be followed by the infinitive "te laver" and make sense: "avant de te laver les mains" (before washing your hands) is the natural question. "Sang" is a noun (blood), "pour" (in order to) is illogical, and "sans te laver" is grammatical but is not the usual question about hand-washing before a meal. Rule: avant de + infinitive. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Pendant les vacances on organise beaucoup de-----------pour valoriser nos cultures.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Festivals" are organised events showing local music, dance and arts, which promote cultures; the plural "festivals" matches "beaucoup de". "Festives" is an adjective, and "festins" are big meals, which do not promote culture. "Fêtes" is possible, but "festivals" is the word that is specifically cultural. Rule: festival = cultural event. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Papa m'a acheté des chaussures----------------.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Marron" is a noun used as a colour adjective, so it is invariable: "des chaussures marron". Adding -s or the feminine ending is wrong. Rule: colour adjectives derived from nouns (marron, orange) do not agree. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: ---------courir, il sera en retard.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Avoir beau + infinitive" expresses concession (although he runs, in vain): "Il a beau courir, il sera en retard". "Bien" and "bel" do not form a concession with an infinitive, and "bel et bien" means really and truly. Rule: avoir beau + infinitive = however much one does something. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Peut-on vraiment étudier ________ la télévision ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The gerund "en regardant" expresses simultaneity (studying while watching TV). "Regardant" without "en" is a participle that cannot link to "étudier" here, "regarder" is an infinitive and cannot follow without a preposition, and "au regard de" means in view of. Rule: gerund = en + present participle. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Maimouna-------------- très tôt ce matin.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Ce matin" requires a past event completed this morning, so the passé composé is used; the auxiliary of a pronominal verb is "être" and the participle agrees with the reflexive pronoun, feminine here (Maimouna): "s'est lavée". "S'était lavé(e)" is the pluperfect, which would need another past action, and "s'est lavé" lacks the agreement. Rule: the participle of a pronominal verb agrees with the preceding direct object. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Il nous a dit qu'il voulait ____ le proviseur.
questions.corrige_markdown: After "voulait", a verb in the infinitive is needed: "voir" (to see). "Voit" is conjugated, and "voix" (voice) and "voie" (way) are nouns that are pronounced the same. Rule: vouloir + infinitive. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Si ces élèves étudiaient, ils ____ à leur examen.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Si" + imperfect ("étudiaient") calls for the present conditional in the main clause: "ils réussiraient". "Réussirent" is the past historic, "réussissent" the present and "réussiront" the future. Rule: si + imparfait -> conditionnel présent. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Penses-tu à ton avenir ? Oui, ------------pense.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Penser à" + a thing is replaced by the pronoun "y": "j'y pense". "En" replaces "de", and "le" and "lui" are used for direct objects or persons. Rule: y replaces à + thing. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: As-tu acheté tes livres ? -Oui, j'en ai acheté -----------------.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Livres" is masculine plural, and after "en" the quantity word stands alone as a pronoun: "certains". "Quelques" cannot be used without a noun, "certaines" is feminine and "certain" is singular. Rule: the indefinite pronoun agrees with the noun it replaces. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Le médecin a recommandé que la grand-mère ------------ régulièrement ses médicaments.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Recommander que" expresses a wish or advice and is followed by the subjunctive: "que la grand-mère prenne". "Prend" (indicative), "prendra" (future) and "doit prendre" (which cannot follow "que" here) are wrong. Rule: recommander que + subjonctif. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: -------------- ordinateur m'a coûté bien cher.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Ordinateur" is masculine and begins with a vowel, so the demonstrative adjective takes the form "cet". "Ce" is used before a masculine noun starting with a consonant, "cette" is feminine and "c'est" is a verb phrase. Rule: ce becomes cet before a masculine noun beginning with a vowel. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: « Les tonneaux vides font trop de bruit » veut dire :
questions.corrige_markdown: The proverb says that those who talk the most have the least to say, so the lesson is to speak little. Options B, C and D claim the opposite (that talkative people are wise). A is the only one that fits the moral. Rule: proverb = empty vessels make the most noise. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Celui qui parle beaucoup a la sagesse.
Celui qui est sage doit faire trop de bruit.
En parlant beaucoup on devient sage.

questions.enonce_markdown: Si tu____ à temps, tu aurais sauvé la vie de cet enfant.
questions.corrige_markdown: The main clause is a past conditional ("tu aurais sauvé"), so the "si" clause takes the pluperfect: "si tu étais venu". The other forms (passé composé, present, imperfect) do not match. Rule: si + plus-que-parfait -> conditionnel passé. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Après ------------, les mariés se sont rendus à l'église.
questions.corrige_markdown: After "après", the past infinitive is used: "être" + participle for a pronominal verb. The couple ("les mariés") is masculine plural, so the participle is "habillés": "s'être habillés". Option A is feminine, B uses an infinitive instead of the participle and D has the wrong auxiliary "avoir". Option C is printed with a capital S, which is a printing slip, but it is the only grammatical form. Rule: après + infinitif passé, with agreement of the participle. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Donne cette lettre à ta tante ! - Oui, je -------------donnerai.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Cette lettre" is a feminine direct object ("la") and "à ta tante" an indirect object ("lui"). When both pronouns are used with a third person, the order is direct before indirect: "je la lui donnerai". "Le lui" is masculine, and "le la" and "lui la" are not possible. Rule: la/le/les come before lui/leur. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: « Des bandits avaient agressé mes sœurs. » A la voix passive cette phrase devient :
questions.corrige_markdown: In the passive, the object becomes the subject and the verb keeps the same tense, with "être" put in that tense and the past participle of the verb. "Avaient agressé" (pluperfect) becomes "avaient été agressées" and the participle agrees with "mes sœurs". Option A is imperfect, C is conditional past and D is passé composé. Rule: the tense is kept in the passive. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

choix.texte: Mes sœurs étaient agressées par des bandits.
Mes sœurs avaient été agressées par des bandits.
Mes sœurs auraient été agressées par des bandits.
Mes sœurs ont été agressées par des bandits

questions.enonce_markdown: '' My parents wanted me to become a medical doctor.'' Can be translated into French as:
questions.corrige_markdown: "Vouloir que" requires the subjunctive, and the English sentence is in the past (wanted), so the main verb is "voulaient", followed by "que je devienne". Option A uses the indicative, C the past historic and D the wrong tense of the main verb (present, not past). Rule: vouloir que + subjonctif. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - translation into French
O Level French - tenses and moods

choix.texte: Mes parents voulaient que je deviens médecin.
Mes parents voulaient que je devienne médecin.
Mes parents voulaient que je devins médecin.
Mes parents veulent que je devienne médecin.

questions.enonce_markdown:
« Si, l'informatique a vraiment changé le monde » Cette phrase est la bonne réponse à la question suivante :

*Options as printed:* A) L'informatique a changé le monde ? B) Est-ce que l'informatique a changé le monde ? C) Le monde est-il changé par l'informatique ? D) L'informatique n'a-t-elle pas changé le monde ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The printed phrase starts with "Si", which can be read in two ways, so the question is ambiguous. Taken as the affirmative "si" (yes, in answer to a negative question), the matching question is D, "L'informatique n'a-t-elle pas changé le monde ?". Taken as the conjunction "si" (whether, in an indirect question), the matching direct question is A or B, which are both correct direct questions on the same fact. Option C changes the meaning by turning the sentence into a passive. Because D, A and B are all defensible, no letter is designated. Rule: "si" is the affirmative answer to a negative question.
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Passage for questions 46 to 50**

*Les questions 46 à 50 portent sur le passage suivant. Vous choisirez vos réponses dans les listes proposées (ABCD).*

Paa Tom est (46). Il se lève très tôt tous les jours pour aller au champ. Avant d'y aller, il donne à (47) oiseaux de la basse cour. Il coupe (48) pour les moutons et chèvres. Puis il prend son (49) et s'en va.

Le soir, il rentre tout fatigué, prend (50), mange et va se coucher.

Blank (46) :
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage says that Paa Tom gets up early to go to the field and feeds poultry, sheep and goats, which is the life of a farmer: "cultivateur". A carpenter (menuisier), a schoolteacher (maitre d'école) and a coppersmith (chaudronnier) do not work in fields. Rule: the context (champ, basse-cour, moutons) gives the profession. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

Blank (47) : « il donne à (47) oiseaux de la basse cour »
questions.corrige_markdown: "Oiseaux" is masculine plural, and the preposition "à" combines with the article "les" to form the contracted "aux": "il donne aux oiseaux". "À le" and "à les" are never written like this, and "à u" is not a French form. Rule: à + les = aux. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

Blank (48) : « Il coupe (48) pour les moutons et chèvres. »

*Options as printed:* A) des branches B) de l'herbe C) les herbes D) l'herbe
questions.corrige_markdown: Three options fit grammatically and in meaning: "Il coupe des branches" (goats and sheep eat leaves), "Il coupe de l'herbe" (partitive, the most natural for feeding sheep) and "Il coupe l'herbe" (definite article). Only "les herbes" (C) is less natural. Because several printed options are defensible, no letter is designated. Rule: couper + partitive or definite article for a plant used as fodder.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

Blank (49) : « Puis il prend son (49) et s'en va. »
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence comes just after the early-morning scene (he gets up very early and goes to the field), so the meal he takes before leaving is the breakfast: "son petit déjeuner". "Souper" and "dîner" are evening meals (he eats in the evening, see blank 50), and "déjeuner" (lunch, midday) does not suit an early start. Rule: morning meal = petit déjeuner. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

Blank (50) : « Le soir, il rentre tout fatigué, prend (50), mange et va se coucher. »

*Options as printed:* A) toilette B) bain C) bouteille D) douche
questions.corrige_markdown: After coming home tired in the evening, a person washes before eating and sleeping: "prend un bain", "prend une douche" and, in a looser sense, "fait sa toilette" are all possible. No determiner is printed in the passage to decide between them, so more than one option is defensible and no letter is designated. "Bouteille" (bottle) is the only option that is clearly wrong. Rule: se laver = prendre un bain ou une douche.
